The Council's plan, widely perceived as a rebuke to Mamdani’s proposal from last month, shows that the city doesn't need to broadly "tax the rich" to close its budget gap.

While not perfect, its budget plan is more pro-growth than the mayor's, @JKetcham91 and Christian Browne write for @CityJournal: city-journal.org/article/new…

Only 0.7% of people filing taxes in New York made over $1 million in 2023, yet they paid 41% of all state income taxes.

The City Council seems to recognize that the NYC will put its future at risk by imposing ever-more taxation on the high earners and corporations that employ millions of New Yorkers.

Kevin Wallsten writes for @CityJournal about how transparency shattered higher education—and how it can also rebuild it.

27 of Yale’s 43 undergraduate departments have zero Republicans on faculty. 

Harvard gives A’s to more than 60% of students, up from 25% in 2005.

Deplatforming is widespread and a significant number of students are hostile to opposing views.

Admissions data from Harvard and Columbia show the real impact of affirmative action in admissions. 

The public isn't losing faith in universities—it's seeing them clearly for the first time.
